subject: Region routing, subprocessors, and deletion/tombstone procedure — PulseAI Q&A
messages:
From: Samir Patel <samir@pulseai.com>

Cc: Lydia Gomez <lydia.gomez@pulseai.com>
Date: Sun, 13 Dec 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Questions on where customer data is processed + deletion flow

Hi Jordan,

Thanks for the demo last week — PulseAI is evaluating Redwood for inference of PII-containing customer transcripts. Before we move to a short PoC we'd like to confirm a few things about processing locality and deletion guarantees:

1) Which regions could my requests be processed in for the hosted product? Will requests ever leave the US (eu/us fallback situations)?
2) Who are the subprocessors involved in request handling and encrypted storage (we need vendor names + high-level roles)?
3) If we request deletion, what is the "tombstone"/purge process end-to-end and how long until we can get an auditable confirmation?

Can you send a short, non-legal answer we can share with our security/compliance team? We may follow up with a more formal questionnaire.

Thanks,
Samir

samir@pulseai.com

Subject: Re: Questions on where customer data is processed + deletion flow

Hi Samir — great question, thanks. High-level answers below so your security team has something concise to review. I've attached a short routing diagram and a privacy quicksheet for reference (see attachments).

Quick answers (summary):
- Regions: Hosted requests for US customers are pinned to our US regions by default (primary: us-east-1). We maintain fallbacks in us-west-2 and eu-west-1 only for capacity/failover or if your routing policy selects multi-region. We do not route production traffic to APAC for US-only customers unless explicitly requested.
- Subprocessors: Storage and long-term logs use cloud providers (AWS/GCP) in the selected region; colocation and networking partners (e.g., Equinix) for edge handoffs; secrets/KMS typically integrate with AWS KMS or customer-managed KMS (HKDF + HSM-backed providers). We will provide a vendor inventory CSV on request.
- Deletion / tombstone: We perform logical deletion (mark/tombstone) immediately on request and remove primary customer data from active stores within 24 hours. Backups and replicated caches follow a staged purge window — typically up to 30 days for hosted customers. We provide audit logs showing deletion events; for Dedicated/Private customers we can shorten windows and support custom erasure procedures.

If helpful, Ben (cc'd) can add the subprocessor list and a couple of implementation details (backup retention specifics and the audit attestation process). We'll also upload the routing diagram to a shared folder for Lydia to review.

Next steps: if PulseAI needs a formal deletion SLA or a certificate-of-deletion workflow, we can put that in the DPA addendum.

Best,
Jordan Blake
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
jordan.blake@redwood.com

Subject: Re: Questions on where customer data is processed + deletion flow

Hi Samir — adding a few technical specifics so you have something to hand to your infra/security folks.

Subprocessor inventory (high-level):
- Compute / inference runtime: AWS (EC2/GPU instances in us-east-1, us-west-2) and GCP (for customers who pick GCP-backed deployment) — role: model execution + ephemeral KV cache.
- Object storage: AWS S3 / GCS depending on region — role: artifact, logs, and longer-term payload storage.
- Networking / edge handoffs: Equinix (colocation) and Cloudflare (egress/proxy) — role: low-latency ingress/egress.
- Secrets & key management: AWS KMS, Google KMS, and customer-managed HSMs / HashiCorp Vault (optional) — role: envelope keys and signing.
- Backup & recovery: Managed snapshot service provided via cloud provider snapshots; long-term archival is encrypted blobs on cloud object storage.

Cross-border behavior:
- Default policy: route and process in the customer-selected region (US for PulseAI) and avoid cross-border movement of request payloads.
- Failover: in cases of capacity outage we may route to a partner region in the same geopolitical area (US to US). We only route to EU/APAC if you request multi-region or if you selected a multi-region resilience policy.
- Third-party subprocessors may have support teams in other regions for maintenance — access is controlled and logged; where required we provide subprocessors' SOC2/ISO attestations.

Deletion/tombstone lifecycle (hosted product):
1) Customer requests deletion via console/API — request triggers immediate tombstone marker in primary index (within minutes).
2) Active store purge: background jobs remove primary copies within 24 hours.
3) Cache eviction: in-memory/KV caches evict on a TTL/eviction schedule (real-time where possible).
4) Backups and snapshots: snapshots are on a rolling retention; hosted default is "7-day snapshot retention" with a 30-day backup window for replicated systems (final physical removal during compaction within 30 days).
5) Final physical purge: background compaction and low-level storage GC complete physical deletion (may take up to 30 days).
6) Audit trail: deletion events (API call, tombstone timestamp, purge completion records) are written to immutable audit logs; we can issue a deletion attestation summarizing the events.

Notes: Dedicated or Private deployments can have custom retention/purge SLAs (we often support 0–7 day backup retention and can schedule immediate scrub windows).

Attaching the subprocessor inventory CSV and will share the Drive folder with supporting evidence.

Cheers,
Ben Carter
Lead Infra PM, Redwood Inference
ben.carter@redwood.com

Attachments: subprocessor-inventory.csv

Jordan/Ben — thanks, that was helpful. A couple of follow-ups from our legal/compliance lead: 

- Backup retention: you mentioned a 7-day snapshot default and a 30-day replication window. Can you confirm whether backups are immutable for the retention window and whether they are overwritten or purged after the window?
- Audit evidence: when you issue a "deletion attestation" what does it contain? Is there a machine-verifiable audit log we can pull or do you provide a signed PDF attestation?
- Emergency restore: if we request data deletion but later need a short restore for investigatory purposes, what is the guaranteed window during which a restore is possible (and does that extend any retention period)?

Also, PulseAI requires an SLA that deletion confirmations are provided within 10 business days of a deletion request for hosted customers. Is Redwood comfortable including that in the DPA?

Thanks — if easier we can take this to a brief call.

Lydia Gomez
Lead Counsel, PulseAI
lydia.gomez@pulseai.com

Subject: Re: Questions on where customer data is processed + deletion flow

Hi Lydia — thanks for the follow-ups. Answers below and proposed next steps. (Quoting Ben's note for clarity.)

- Backup immutability and purge: Hosted snapshots are treated as encrypted objects with standard provider snapshot semantics. For the hosted plan we overwrite/purge snapshots as soon as the retention window elapses (default: 7-day immutable snapshot window followed by staged compaction up to 30 days). We can add an addendum to the DPA to make the exact retention window contractual.

- Deletion attestation / audit evidence: we provide both options: (1) a machine-readable audit export (immutable log entries with timestamps, API request ID, and object identifiers) and (2) a signed PDF attestation that summarizes the timeline and includes a cryptographic hash of the audit export for verification. For customers that need ongoing access to logs we offer a read-only log export (S3/GCS) for a limited window.

- Emergency restore window: for hosted customers the practical restore window is up to the backup retention period (default 7–30 days depending on snapshot replication). If you expect to need restores beyond that period we recommend a Dedicated deployment or a custom archive policy; we can also implement a hold/escrow flow for specific datasets. Any restore operation will be logged and will extend no automatic retention unless explicitly requested.

- SLA: Redwood can commit to providing deletion confirmation/attestation within 10 business days for hosted customers as a DPA addendum. For Dedicated/Private deployments we can negotiate shorter windows.
